questions.question: What is the expected major product when Ribonucleic acid (RNA) is treated with Dilute aqueous sodium hydroxide (0.1 M NaOH)?

options.label: B
options.text: Stable (denatures to single strands without backbone cleavage)

questions.explanation: Treating Ribonucleic acid (RNA) with Dilute aqueous sodium hydroxide (0.1 M NaOH) yields Mixture of 2'- and 3'-nucleoside monophosphates. Rationale: The 2'-hydroxyl group attacks the adjacent 3'-phosphodiester bond, forming a cyclic 2',3'-phosphate intermediate.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) into Stable (denatures to single strands without backbone cleavage)?

options.label: C
options.text: Dilute aqueous sodium hydroxide (0.1 M NaOH)

questions.correct_answer: Dilute aqueous sodium hydroxide (0.1 M NaOH)
questions.explanation: To convert Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) into Stable (denatures to single strands without backbone cleavage), the appropriate reagent is Dilute aqueous sodium hydroxide (0.1 M NaOH). Rationale: DNA lacks a 2'-hydroxyl group, making its phosphodiester backbone completely resistant to alkaline cleavage.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Primer-template DNA duplex is treated with DNA Polymerase + 4 dNTPs (dATP, dCTP, dGTP, dTTP)?
questions.explanation: Treating Primer-template DNA duplex with DNA Polymerase + 4 dNTPs (dATP, dCTP, dGTP, dTTP) yields Extended double-stranded DNA + Pyrophosphate (PPi). Rationale: 3'-Hydroxyl of the growing primer attacks the alpha-phosphate of incoming dNTP, releasing pyrophosphate.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of DNA sequencing reaction mixture into DNA fragments terminating selectively at dideoxy-A?

options.label: A
options.text: Dilute aqueous sodium hydroxide (0.1 M NaOH)

questions.explanation: To convert DNA sequencing reaction mixture into DNA fragments terminating selectively at dideoxy-A, the appropriate reagent is DNA Polymerase + dNTPs + ddATP (2',3'-dideoxy). Rationale: ddATP lacks both 2'-OH and 3'-OH groups; once incorporated, no further phosphodiester bond can form.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when 5'-DMT-nucleoside phosphoramidite is treated with 3'-Anchored nucleoside + Tetrazole catalyst?

options.label: D
options.text: Doubled quantity of target duplex DNA

questions.explanation: Treating 5'-DMT-nucleoside phosphoramidite with 3'-Anchored nucleoside + Tetrazole catalyst yields Phosphite triester intermediate. Rationale: Tetrazole protonates the diisopropylamino group, facilitating nucleophilic attack by the 5'-hydroxyl of the growing chain.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Phosphite triester into Stable phosphate triester backbone?
questions.explanation: To convert Phosphite triester into Stable phosphate triester backbone, the appropriate reagent is Iodine (I2) in THF, pyridine, H2O. Rationale: Iodine oxidizes phosphorus(III) to phosphorus(V), generating the stable phosphate triester linkage.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with 3% Trichloroacetic acid (TCA) in CH2Cl2 to yield 5'-Unprotected hydroxyl + DMT cation (bright orange) as the major product?
questions.explanation: 5'-Dimethoxytrityl (DMT)-protected nucleotide reacts with 3% Trichloroacetic acid (TCA) in CH2Cl2 to yield 5'-Unprotected hydroxyl + DMT cation (bright orange). Rationale: Mild acid cleaves the acid-sensitive trityl ether, releasing the resonance-stabilized orange dimethoxytrityl carbocation.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Double-stranded genomic DNA is treated with Heat (95°C for 30 seconds)?

options.label: A
options.text: Doubled quantity of target duplex DNA

questions.explanation: Treating Double-stranded genomic DNA with Heat (95°C for 30 seconds) yields Two separated single-stranded DNA templates. Rationale: Thermal energy disrupts hydrogen bonds between Watson-Crick base pairs, separating the duplex strands.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with Specific oligonucleotide primers (55°C) to yield Primer-template duplex hybrids as the major product?
questions.explanation: Single-stranded template DNA reacts with Specific oligonucleotide primers (55°C) to yield Primer-template duplex hybrids. Rationale: Lowering temperature allows complementary oligonucleotide primers to hybridize specifically to target flanking regions.
